factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.90–0.97) of Token split, Number of empty sequence flows, Control flow complexity, Size and Coefficient of network connectivity, with Maximum connector degree (0.76) and Connector Mismatch (0.55), describe how large a net is and how much splitting and parallel structure it contains. Density loads moderately negatively (-0.46), consistent with larger nets being sparser. Maximum connector degree also loads 0.39 on Factor 2, and Connector Mismatch has a low communality (0.35).

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89) and Density (0.84) load highly, while Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.58). This suggests nets with high-degree connectors in a dense structure that tend to use a single connector type. Connector Heterogeneity has a low communality (0.35) and Density also loads -0.46 on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.96) and Separability (0.69) load on this factor, describing nets made largely of plain sequences with many articulation points. The factor rests on only two measures, and Sequentiality is a possible Heywood case (communality 1.017).

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. Three varimax-rotated factors explain 82% of the variance, in line with the three eigenvalues above 1. Factor 1 is a dominant size and branching dimension (49%). Factor 2 captures connector degree and density (17%). Factor 3 captures sequential, separable structure (16%). No cross-loadings beyond the 0.15 gap are flagged and every measure is assigned.
caveats: Sequentiality has a communality above 1 (possible Heywood case), so its loading and Factor 3 should be read cautiously.
Factor 3 rests on only two measures.
Connector Mismatch and Connector Heterogeneity have low communalities (about 0.35), so they are only weakly represented by the solution.
Connector Heterogeneity, Average connector degree and Density have MSA values just above 0.6.
Number of duplicate tasks was removed as constant, so this solution says nothing about duplicate labels.
The factors reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the number of factors.
